EDIT: I just posted this bug and my thoughts here as an issue on the github page for tracking purposes: https://github.com/voat/voat/issues/683

Line 243 actually calls Utils.User.DailyCrossPostingQuotaUsed(User.Identity.Name, submission.MessageContent).

DailyCrossPostingQuotaUsed is defined here. The parameters take in a username and URL. I believe this code branch just checks if the same URL was posted within the past 24 hours by this user. Edit: And further checks if the count exceeds the DailyCrossPostingQuota app setting which is pulled from web.config (which is currently set to 2 according to what's in the repo).
Oh you're absolutely correct, I flat out misread that. Good catch!

Maybe something wrong with how date/time is used? Especially when it comes to retrieving the Date value for Message DB records? UTC isn't used anywhere; it's all local server time, which makes datetime processing problems like this that much easier to come across.

When pulled from the DB, I believe Message.Date property is going to be a DateTime but with the "kind" property set to DateTimeKind.Unspecified by default. Where as when a new date is created in code with DateTime.Now, I believe it's "kind" is going to be DateTimeKind.Local. I'm not sure, but I don't think you can actually get accurate results comparing two DateTime objects with different "kind" settings. Maybe somehow calling DateTime.SpecifyKind on Message.Date property to at least mark it as "local" as soon as a record is pulled from the DB and before even using it elsewhere in any comparison code.

I don't know. Maybe I'm way off.

Edit: There will always be pitfalls working with standard DateTime types especially when not working strictly in UTC in all areas. Further, specifying the "kind" property on Date column once extracted from the DB may actually screw things up further if under the hood it applies a timezone adjustment to the datetime value... or it may not.

I would love if all date values get converted over to UTC. That would mean less headaches especially if there are multiple instances of the application running all over the world in any distributed setup. On the other hand, I realize making the switch now would be painful for devs.
